transfers.source_mechanism: Flow-dependent reinforcement of transport structures through positive feedback
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Traffic flow-dependent reinforcement of signal timing through local positive feedback enables adaptive optimization of traffic networks without central coordination.
transfers.required_translation: Replace rhythmic contraction with signal green phase timing, structural thickening with increased green time allocation, structural thinning with decreased green time allocation, and flow-dependent adaptation with traffic-responsive signal timing adjustments. Replace material availability with computational resources at each intersection controller.
transfers.expected_effect: Development of an adaptive traffic signal network that self-optimizes based on local traffic conditions, converging to efficient flow patterns without central coordination.
boundary_conditions: sufficient traffic flow to trigger adaptation
limited communication range between adjacent intersections
bounded computational capacity at each intersection
failure_conditions: extremely low traffic flow preventing adaptation
excessive computational load preventing real-time decisions
transfers.testable_prediction: After implementing the adaptive signal system, average intersection delay will decrease by at least 15% during peak hours compared to the current 6-month-optimized plan, while maintaining stability (no oscillations) during simulated incident scenarios.
